name: RelativityOne
description: RelativityOne is a cloud e-discovery and legal data platform for investigations, review, legal hold, collection, processing, analytics, productions, user and workspace administration, reporting, and litigation support.
agentUseSummary: RelativityOne is visible as a preview-only Marketplace entry. Relativity publishes extensive REST APIs and documents OAuth2 client-credentials bearer-token authentication, but the reviewed public materials require instance-specific hosts, administrator-created OAuth2 clients, an administrator Context User, and broad workspace, user, object, document, processing, legal hold, analytics, production, and administration APIs. Relay will not collect Relativity usernames/passwords, cookies, admin OAuth client secrets, or instance identifiers, and will not mount a broad RelativityOne API connector until the exact customer tenant authorizes a least-privilege integration contract and a safe V1 authority boundary.

capabilities.label: Coordinate e-discovery operations
capabilities.description: Preview a future exact-instance-authorized, least-privilege integration surface without assuming access to identity, workspace, document, matter, legal hold, analytics, production, or administration records.

blocked.label: Connect without a RelativityOne instance contract
blocked.description: Relay will not accept or mint credentials until the exact customer tenant authorizes Relay and supplies the approved instance host, OAuth2 client, Context User, scopes, permission model, token lifecycle, audit obligations, test workspace, and production acceptance process.

blocked.label: Access identity, workspace, or user data
blocked.description: Instance identifiers, clients, matters, workspaces, users, groups, permissions, workspace access, item security, login profiles, settings, and administration records remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Access documents, objects, legal hold, or review data
blocked.description: Documents, object manager data, custodians, legal hold, collection, processing, review, productions, analytics, search indexes, pivots, notifications, billing insights, usage reports, and related legal data remain blocked.

blocked.label: Use basic auth, cookies, admin clients, or raw APIs
blocked.description: Usernames, passwords, RelAuth cookies, browser sessions, administrator Context User clients, generic Relativity REST endpoints, Object Manager queries, SOQL-like object exploration, arbitrary instance hosts, pagination tokens, bulk operations, exports, writes, and administration are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Instance and administrator review required
approvalProfiles.description: No agent action is callable until the exact RelativityOne tenant, administrator, and customer security owner authorize a least-privilege Relay integration and live acceptance boundary.

runtimeSupport.description: RelativityOne remains visible for discovery, but no OpenClaw tools are callable before exact-instance authorization, administrator/security review, least-privilege design, and live acceptance.
RelativityOne remains visible for discovery, but no Hermes tools are callable before exact-instance authorization, administrator/security review, least-privilege design, and live acceptance.

providerSetup.blocker: Relativity publishes REST APIs and OAuth2 client-credentials authentication, but the public materials require instance-specific hosts and administrator-created OAuth2 clients with an administrator Context User. The reviewed materials do not define a Relay-approved least-privilege V1 authority endpoint or production acceptance contract for a safe connector.
providerSetup.nextAction: Obtain explicit approval from the exact RelativityOne customer tenant and administrator/security owner. Define a customer-approved OAuth2 client, Context User, scopes, permission model, test workspace, fixed identity-free authority endpoint, token lifecycle, audit obligations, rate handling, disconnect behavior, and live acceptance before implementing any connector.

evidence.supports: Relativity documents REST authentication through basic auth, browser RelAuth cookies, Active Directory, and OAuth2 client-credentials bearer tokens created in the OAuth2 Client Manager with a Context User who is a Relativity Administrators group member.
RelativityOne publishes many platform APIs for tasks that users perform manually in the UI, including workspaces, users, and other broad platform operations.

RelativityOne REST references cover broad services including billing insights, Collect, conceptual analytics, import, legal hold, automated workflows, review, identity, imaging, mass operations, notifications, Object Manager, processing, productions, telemetry, and usage reports.
Relativity's first REST call guide requires access to a RelativityOne instance and its unique domain identifier before making API calls.

securityNotes: No RelativityOne instance host, username, password, RelAuth cookie, OAuth client ID, client secret, access token, workspace identifier, user, document, object, legal hold, processing, analytics, production, or legal data was collected or tested.

The existence of public Relativity REST APIs does not establish Relay authorization for any customer instance, administrator Context User, workspace, Object Manager surface, document set, or legal matter.

Relay will not use basic authentication, Active Directory credentials, browser cookies, administrator OAuth clients, arbitrary instance hosts, Object Manager queries, pagination tokens, bulk exports, or raw REST exploration as a substitute for exact-instance approval.

All identity, workspace, user, group, permission, client, matter, document, object, legal hold, collection, processing, review, production, analytics, billing, usage, write, administration, raw API, pagination, bulk, and export operations remain unavailable.
